data.long_meaning: The name Raimundo is derived from the Latin word 'Raimundus', which means 'recommender' or 'counselor'. It is a name of deep meaning rooted in the Christian tradition. In the Bible, Raimundo is associated with the saint of the same name, who was a Viscount of Toulouse in the 11th century. He was known for his wisdom and his strong faith, and he was a great advocate for the poor. Raimundo's legacy continues to inspire those who seek to help others and to provide guidance and counsel in times of need.

in_hebrew.name: רימונדו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רימונדו הוא שם שמקורו בשפה הגרמנית ומשמעותו 'עוזר חזק להגנת העם'. השם נגזר משתי מילים: 'רגיס', שפירושה 'עוזר' או 'מועיל', ו'מונד', שפירושה 'מגן' או 'הגנה'. למרות שלא מופיע ישירות בכתבי הקודש, השם קשור למושגים של הגנה וסיוע, שהם מרכזיים בערכים הנוצריים.

in_greek.name: Ραϊμούνδο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ραϊμούνδο προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'ισχυρός προστάτης του λαού'. Αυτό το όνομα αποτελείται από δύο λέξεις: 'regis', που σημαίνει 'βοηθός' ή 'χρήσιμος', και 'mund', που σημαίνει 'ασπίδα' ή 'προστασία'. Αν και δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα στα Ιερά Κείμενα, το όνομα συνδέεται με έννοιες προστασίας και βοήθειας, που είναι θεμελιώδεις στις χριστιανικές αξίες.

in_latin.name: Raimundus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Raimundus origine germanica ortum est et significat 'validus protector populi'. Hoc nomen ex duabus vocibus constat: 'regis', quod significat 'adiutor' vel 'utilis', et 'mund', quod significat 'scutum' vel 'protectorium'. Quamvis non directe in Scripturis Sacris appareat, nomen tamen coniungitur cum conceptibus protectionis et auxilii, quae sunt fundamentalia in valoribus christianis.

Historically, the name has been used in various Christian cultures, symbolizing strength and guardianship.

historical_references.reference: Raimundo de Borgoña, also known as Raymond of Burgundy, was a 13th-century Christian military leader who played a significant role in the Crusades. He led the Crusader army in the successful siege of Acre in 1191, which was a major turning point in the Third Crusade.

Raimundo de Tui, also known as Raymond of Tui, was a 15th-century Christian navigator and explorer who is believed to have led the first European expedition to explore the coast of present-day Brazil. He set sail from Portugal in 1499, over a decade before Christopher Columbus's first voyage.
